questions.scenario: The base sequence of part of the template strand of a DNA molecule is: TAC TTG GGA ACT. The table shows some mRNA codons and the amino acids they code for.
questions.scenarioAf: Die basisvolgorde van ’n deel van die templaatstring van ’n DNS-molekule is: TAC TTG GGA ACT. Die tabel toon sommige mRNS-kodons en die aminosure waarvoor hulle kodeer.

questions.q: Write down the mRNA sequence formed from this template strand.
questions.qAf: Skryf die mRNS-volgorde neer wat vanaf hierdie templaatstring gevorm word.
points: AUG AAC CCU UGA
pointsAf: AUG AAC CCU UGA

questions.q: Write down the anticodon of the tRNA that brings the second amino acid.
questions.qAf: Skryf die antikodon neer van die tRNS wat die tweede aminosuur bring.
points: UUG
pointsAf: UUG

questions.q: Use the table to give the sequence of amino acids coded for by this part of the DNA.
questions.qAf: Gebruik die tabel om die volgorde van aminosure te gee waarvoor hierdie deel van die DNS kodeer.
points: methionine – asparagine – proline (UGA is a stop codon)
pointsAf: metionien – asparagien – prolien (UGA is ’n stopkodon)

questions.q: Name the process in which mRNA is made from DNA.
questions.qAf: Noem die proses waarin mRNS vanaf DNS gemaak word.
points: transcription
pointsAf: transkripsie

questions.q: A mutation changes the sixth base of the template strand from G to C. Explain the effect of this mutation on the protein.
questions.qAf: ’n Mutasie verander die sesde basis van die templaatstring van G na C. Verduidelik die uitwerking van hierdie mutasie op die proteïen.
points: The second mRNA codon changes from AAC to AAG
AAG codes for lysine instead of asparagine
a different amino acid may change the shape and function of the protein
pointsAf: Die tweede mRNS-kodon verander van AAC na AAG
AAG kodeer vir lisien in plaas van asparagien
’n ander aminosuur kan die vorm en funksie van die proteïen verander

questions.scenario: Scientists measured the average beak depth of a population of seed-eating finches on an island. During the 1977 drought, mostly large, hard seeds were left. The table shows the results.
questions.scenarioAf: Wetenskaplikes het die gemiddelde snaweldiepte van ’n bevolking saadetende vinke op ’n eiland gemeet. Tydens die droogte van 1977 het hoofsaaklik groot, harde sade oorgebly. Die tabel toon die resultate.

questions.q: What was the average beak depth in 1978?
questions.qAf: Wat was die gemiddelde snaweldiepte in 1978?

questions.q: Describe the change in average beak depth from 1976 to 1978.
questions.qAf: Beskryf die verandering in gemiddelde snaweldiepte vanaf 1976 tot 1978.
points: The average beak depth increased
from 9,2 mm to 10,0 mm
pointsAf: Die gemiddelde snaweldiepte het toegeneem
van 9,2 mm tot 10,0 mm

questions.q: Use the theory of natural selection to explain this change.
questions.qAf: Gebruik die teorie van natuurlike seleksie om hierdie verandering te verduidelik.
points: There was variation in beak depth in the population
during the drought mainly large, hard seeds were available
birds with deeper beaks could crack these seeds, so more of them survived and reproduced
they passed the alleles for deep beaks to their offspring, so the average beak depth increased
pointsAf: Daar was variasie in snaweldiepte in die bevolking
tydens die droogte was hoofsaaklik groot, harde sade beskikbaar
voëls met dieper snawels kon hierdie sade oopbreek, dus het meer van hulle oorleef en voortgeplant
hulle het die allele vir diep snawels aan hul nakomelinge oorgedra, dus het die gemiddelde snaweldiepte toegeneem

questions.q: Suggest why the average beak depth decreased again after the good rains.
questions.qAf: Stel voor waarom die gemiddelde snaweldiepte ná die goeie reën weer afgeneem het.
points: Small, soft seeds became plentiful again
birds with smaller beaks were no longer at a disadvantage (or had an advantage), so more of them survived and reproduced
pointsAf: Klein, sagte sade het weer volop geword
voëls met kleiner snawels was nie meer benadeel nie (of het ’n voordeel gehad), dus het meer van hulle oorleef en voortgeplant

questions.q: Name the part of a flower where meiosis produces pollen grains.
questions.qAf: Noem die deel van ’n blom waar meiose stuifmeelkorrels produseer.

questions.q: Describe the events of anaphase II and telophase II.
questions.qAf: Beskryf die gebeure van anafase II en telofase II.
points: Anaphase II: the centromeres split
the chromatids are pulled to opposite poles by the spindle fibres
Telophase II: nuclear membranes form around the four groups of chromosomes
the cytoplasm divides, forming four haploid cells
pointsAf: Anafase II: die sentromere verdeel
die chromatiede word deur die spoeldrade na teenoorgestelde pole getrek
Telofase II: kernmembrane vorm om die vier groepe chromosome
die sitoplasma deel en vorm vier haploïede selle

questions.q: Explain how crossing over and the random arrangement of chromosomes lead to genetic variation.
questions.qAf: Verduidelik hoe oorkruising en die lukrake rangskikking van chromosome tot genetiese variasie lei.
points: Crossing over exchanges genetic material between chromatids of homologous chromosomes
producing new combinations of alleles
homologous pairs line up randomly at the equator in metaphase I
so many different combinations of chromosomes end up in the gametes
pointsAf: Oorkruising ruil genetiese materiaal tussen chromatiede van homoloë chromosome uit
wat nuwe kombinasies van allele lewer
homoloë pare staan in metafase I lukraak by die ewenaar
dus beland baie verskillende kombinasies van chromosome in die gamete

questions.q: How many chromatids are present in a human cell at the start of prophase I?
questions.qAf: Hoeveel chromatiede is teenwoordig in ’n menslike sel aan die begin van profase I?

questions.qAf: Wat is die waarskynlikheid dat ’n kind van hierdie ouers vas oorlelle het?

questions.q: Explain what is meant by homozygous.
questions.qAf: Verduidelik wat met homosigoties bedoel word.
points: Having two identical alleles
for a characteristic, for example FF or ff

questions.scenario: A man with blood group A (IᴬIᴬ) has children with a woman who has blood group AB (IᴬIᴮ).

questions.q: There are three alleles for the ABO blood groups. Explain why each person has only two of them.
questions.qAf: Daar is drie allele vir die ABO-bloedgroepe. Verduidelik waarom elke persoon net twee daarvan het.
points: The three alleles exist in the population (multiple alleles)
each person has two copies of the chromosome that carries the gene
one inherited from each parent, so only two alleles per person
pointsAf: Die drie allele bestaan in die bevolking (veelvuldige allele)
elke persoon het twee kopieë van die chromosoom wat die geen dra

questions.scenario: A colour-blind woman (XᵇXᵇ) has children with a man who has normal colour vision (XᴮY).
questions.scenarioAf: ’n Kleurblinde vrou (XᵇXᵇ) het kinders met ’n man wat normale kleursig het (XᴮY).

questions.q: Explain why colour blindness is more common in males than in females.
questions.qAf: Verduidelik waarom kleurblindheid meer by mans as by vroue voorkom.
points: Males have only one X chromosome
so one recessive allele is enough for the disorder to show
pointsAf: Mans het net een X-chromosoom
dus is een resessiewe alleel genoeg vir die afwyking om te toon

questions.q: Determine the genotypes of the children and the percentage of sons and daughters who will be colour-blind.
questions.qAf: Bepaal die genotipes van die kinders en die persentasie seuns en dogters wat kleurblind sal wees.
points: Parents: XᵇXᵇ × XᴮY
daughters: XᴮXᵇ
sons: XᵇY
100% of the sons are colour-blind and 0% of the daughters (all are carriers)
pointsAf: Ouers: XᵇXᵇ × XᴮY
dogters: XᴮXᵇ
seuns: XᵇY
100% van die seuns is kleurblind en 0% van die dogters (almal is draers)

questions.q: Could these parents have a colour-blind daughter? Explain.
questions.qAf: Kan hierdie ouers ’n kleurblinde dogter hê? Verduidelik.
points: No
the father always passes his Xᴮ chromosome to his daughters, so they each have one normal allele
pointsAf: Nee
die vader dra altyd sy Xᴮ-chromosoom aan sy dogters oor, dus het elkeen een normale alleel

questions.q: Explain what cloning is.
questions.qAf: Verduidelik wat klonering is.
points: The production of an organism
that is genetically identical to its parent (from a body cell, without fertilisation)
pointsAf: Die produksie van ’n organisme
wat geneties identies aan sy ouer is (uit ’n liggaamsel, sonder bevrugting)

questions.q: Give TWO advantages of cloning animals.
questions.qAf: Gee TWEE voordele van die klonering van diere.
points: many animals with the same desirable characteristics can be produced quickly
endangered species can be preserved
pointsAf: baie diere met dieselfde gewenste eienskappe kan vinnig geproduseer word
bedreigde spesies kan bewaar word

questions.q: Give TWO uses of genetic engineering in agriculture.
questions.qAf: Gee TWEE gebruike van genetiese manipulasie in die landbou.
points: crops that resist insect pests (e.g. Bt maize)
crops that resist drought or herbicides / have better nutritional value
pointsAf: gewasse wat teen insekplae bestand is (bv. Bt-mielies)
gewasse wat teen droogte of onkruiddoders bestand is / beter voedingswaarde het

questions.qAf: Noem die boustene van DNS.

questions.qAf: Noem die basis wat in DNS met adenien paar.
points: thymine
pointsAf: timien

questions.q: Describe the process of transcription.
questions.qAf: Beskryf die proses van transkripsie.
points: The DNA double helix unwinds and the hydrogen bonds between the bases break
one strand acts as a template
free RNA nucleotides attach to the complementary bases (A pairs with U)
forming a strand of mRNA
the mRNA leaves the nucleus through a nuclear pore and goes to a ribosome
pointsAf: Die DNS-dubbelheliks ontrol en die waterstofbindings tussen die basisse breek
een string dien as ’n templaat
vry RNS-nukleotiede heg aan die komplementêre basisse (A paar met U)
en vorm ’n string mRNS
die mRNS verlaat die kern deur ’n kernporie en gaan na ’n ribosoom

questions.q: The genetic code is described as universal. Explain what this means and why it is important.
questions.qAf: Die genetiese kode word as universeel beskryf. Verduidelik wat dit beteken en waarom dit belangrik is.
points: The same codons code for the same amino acids in all organisms
this is evidence that all organisms share a common ancestor
it makes genetic engineering possible, for example human genes can be expressed in bacteria
pointsAf: Dieselfde kodons kodeer vir dieselfde aminosure in alle organismes
dit is ’n bewys dat alle organismes ’n gemeenskaplike voorouer deel
dit maak genetiese manipulasie moontlik, byvoorbeeld menslike gene kan in bakterieë uitgedruk word

questions.q: Define a biological species.
questions.qAf: Definieer ’n biologiese spesie.
points: A group of organisms with similar characteristics
that can interbreed to produce fertile offspring
pointsAf: ’n Groep organismes met soortgelyke eienskappe
wat kan kruisteel om vrugbare nakomelinge te lewer

questions.q: Describe how the different species of finches on the Galápagos Islands may have formed from one ancestral species.
questions.qAf: Beskryf hoe die verskillende spesies vinke op die Galápagos-eilande uit een voorouerlike spesie kon ontstaan het.
points: Ancestral finches reached the islands from the mainland
they spread to different islands and were geographically isolated
so there was no gene flow between the populations
each island had different food sources
natural selection favoured different beak shapes on each island
over many generations the populations became reproductively isolated and formed new species
pointsAf: Voorouerlike vinke het die eilande vanaf die vasteland bereik
hulle het na verskillende eilande versprei en is geografies geïsoleer
dus was daar geen geenvloei tussen die bevolkings nie
elke eiland het verskillende voedselbronne gehad
natuurlike seleksie het verskillende snawelvorms op elke eiland bevoordeel
oor baie geslagte het die bevolkings reproduktief geïsoleer geraak en nuwe spesies gevorm

questions.q: Explain how artificial selection has produced many different breeds of dogs.
questions.qAf: Verduidelik hoe kunsmatige seleksie baie verskillende hondrasse geproduseer het.
points: Humans chose dogs with the characteristics they wanted
and bred only those dogs
this was repeated over many generations
so the desired characteristics became common and distinct breeds formed
pointsAf: Mense het honde met die eienskappe wat hulle wou hê, gekies
en net daardie honde geteel
dit is oor baie geslagte herhaal
dus het die gewenste eienskappe algemeen geword en afsonderlike rasse het gevorm

questions.q: Explain why evolution is called a scientific theory.
questions.qAf: Verduidelik waarom evolusie ’n wetenskaplike teorie genoem word.
points: It is an explanation that is supported by a large body of evidence
and it has been tested and is accepted by the scientific community
pointsAf: Dit is ’n verduideliking wat deur ’n groot hoeveelheid bewyse ondersteun word
en dit is getoets en word deur die wetenskaplike gemeenskap aanvaar

questions.q: Give TWO advantages of bipedalism.
questions.qAf: Gee TWEE voordele van tweevoetigheid.
points: the hands are free to carry objects and use tools
the eyes are higher, so predators and food can be seen over tall grass / less of the body is exposed to the sun

questions.q: Name the species to which the fossil known as Mrs Ples belongs.
questions.qAf: Noem die spesie waaraan die fossiel bekend as Mrs Ples behoort.

questions.q: Explain why the many hominid fossils in the caves of the Cradle of Humankind are important for understanding human evolution.
questions.qAf: Verduidelik waarom die baie hominiedfossiele in die grotte van die Wieg van die Mensdom belangrik is om menslike evolusie te verstaan.
points: There are fossils of several different hominid species
from over millions of years
they show how features such as brain size and bipedalism changed over time
and they support the idea that hominids evolved in Africa (Out of Africa)
pointsAf: Daar is fossiele van verskeie verskillende hominiedspesies
oor miljoene jare
hulle wys hoe kenmerke soos breingrootte en tweevoetigheid oor tyd verander het
en hulle ondersteun die idee dat hominiede in Afrika ontwikkel het (Uit Afrika)

questions.q:
Describe the events of meiosis I and meiosis II, and explain how non-disjunction during meiosis can result in a child with Down syndrome.
Content: 17 Synthesis: 3
NOTE: NO marks will be awarded for answers in the form of flow charts, tables or diagrams.
questions.qAf:
Beskryf die gebeure van meiose I en meiose II, en verduidelik hoe nie-disjunksie tydens meiose kan lei tot ’n kind met Downsindroom.
Inhoud: 17 Sintese: 3
LET WEL: GEEN punte sal toegeken word vir antwoorde in die vorm van vloeidiagramme, tabelle of diagramme nie.
points:
Meiosis I (max 8)
Interphase: the DNA replicates before meiosis
Prophase I: chromosomes condense and become visible as two chromatids
homologous chromosomes pair up
crossing over takes place at the chiasmata
the nuclear membrane disappears and spindle fibres form
Metaphase I: homologous pairs line up randomly at the equator
Anaphase I: homologous chromosomes are pulled to opposite poles
Telophase I: two cells form, each with half the number of chromosomes (haploid)

Meiosis II (max 4)
Metaphase II: chromosomes line up singly at the equator
Anaphase II: the centromeres split and chromatids move to opposite poles
Telophase II: nuclear membranes form
four genetically different haploid cells are produced

Down syndrome (max 5)
Non-disjunction happens when chromosome pair 21 fails to separate in anaphase I
or the chromatids fail to separate in anaphase II
one gamete receives two copies of chromosome 21 and another none
the gamete with two copies is fertilised by a normal gamete
the zygote has three copies of chromosome 21 (trisomy 21), 47 chromosomes in total
the risk increases with the age of the mother
pointsAf:
Meiose I (maks 8)
Interfase: die DNS repliseer voor meiose
Profase I: chromosome kondenseer en word sigbaar as twee chromatiede
homoloë chromosome paar
oorkruising vind by die chiasmata plaas
die kernmembraan verdwyn en spoeldrade vorm
Metafase I: homoloë pare staan lukraak by die ewenaar
Anafase I: homoloë chromosome word na teenoorgestelde pole getrek
Telofase I: twee selle vorm, elk met die helfte van die aantal chromosome (haploïed)

Meiose II (maks 4)
Metafase II: chromosome staan enkel by die ewenaar
Anafase II: die sentromere verdeel en chromatiede beweeg na teenoorgestelde pole
Telofase II: kernmembrane vorm
vier geneties verskillende haploïede selle word geproduseer

Downsindroom (maks 5)
Nie-disjunksie gebeur wanneer chromosoompaar 21 in anafase I nie skei nie
of die chromatiede in anafase II nie skei nie
een gameet ontvang twee kopieë van chromosoom 21 en ’n ander geen
die gameet met twee kopieë word deur ’n normale gameet bevrug
die sigoot het drie kopieë van chromosoom 21 (trisomie 21), altesaam 47 chromosome
die risiko neem toe met die ouderdom van die moeder
